{{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA AmeriCup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2017 FIBA Americas Championship|2017 Argentina]]|}} }} '''Kendall Dewan Marshall''' (born August 19, 1991) is an American former [[basketball]] coach and former professional player. He was born in [[Dumfries, Virginia]], and attended [[Bishop Denis J. O'Connell High School|Bishop O'Connell High School]] in [[Arlington, Virginia]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] and was drafted by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the first round of the [[2012 NBA draft]] with the 13th overall pick. ==Early life== Marshall led [[Bishop O'Connell High School]] to the 2010 Virginia Independent Schools Division I championship as a senior. He also led Bishop O'Connell to the semifinals of the Washington Catholic Athletic Conference. He averaged 15.3 points, nine rebounds and six assists as a senior. Considered a four-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Marshall was listed as the No. 7 point guard and the No. 22 player in the nation in 2010.{{cite web |title=Kendall Marshall Recruiting Profile |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/44029 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}} ==College career== ===Freshman season=== At the start of his first season at North Carolina, Marshall provided more depth at the point guard position to relieve starting point guard [[Larry Drew II]], as he got more used to the system at North Carolina. However, after a disappointing showing at [[2010–11 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]] in which the Tar Heels lost by twenty points, [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] took the gamble and inserted Marshall into the starting lineup at a win versus [[2010–11 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]].{{Cite web |title=North Carolina 64-62 Clemson (Feb 12, 2011) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore/_/gameId/310430228 |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=ESPN |language=en}} Soon Drew transferred to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], allowing Marshall to take on the leadership role with poise; as he dished out an ACC-record 16 assists while committing only three turnovers at a win over [[2010–11 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] on February 6, 2011.{{Cite web |title=North Carolina 89-69 Florida State (Feb 6, 2011) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/310370153 |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Marshall averaged 6.2 points and 6.2 assists per game. ===Sophomore season=== Marshall had an excellent sophomore season in which he set the all time UNC assist record of 351, surpassing former UNC point guard [[Ed Cota]] as the all-time leader in assists in a single season in school history. On March 9, 2012, Marshall set another record, the all-time ACC record in assists in a single season with 311, surpassing the previous record set by former [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] point guard [[Craig Neal]].{{cite web |last=Katz |first=Andy |author-link=Andy Katz |date=2011-03-16 |title=Kendall Marshall gains confidence |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/tournament/2011/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=6224000 |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=ESPN.com}}{{Cite web |title=North Carolina 85-69 Maryland (Mar 9, 2012) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/320690153 |access-date=2024-03-06 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Marshall fractured his wrist during North Carolina's NCAA tournament win against [[2011–12 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]], landing hard after being fouled while driving for a layup.{{cite web |last=Gardiner |first=Andy |date=2012-03-19 |title=Kendall Marshall fractures right wrist as UNC beats Creighton |url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/campusrivalry/post/2012/03/uncs-kendall-marshall-fractures-right-wrist/1#.T_ZeevWDmSo |access-date=March 6, 2024 |publisher=content.usatoday.com}} He did not return for the remainder of the season, as Carolina fell to [[2011–12 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] in the regional finals. Marshall won the 2012 Bob Cousy award, joining past winners [[Raymond Felton]] (2005) and [[Ty Lawson]] (2009) as Tar Heels who have won the award.{{cite web |last=Barbour |first=Brian |date=March 29, 2012 |title=Kendall Marshall Wins Bob Cousy Award |url=https://www.tarheelblog.com/2012/03/kendall-marshall-wins-bob-cousy-award |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=TarHeelBlog.com}} As a sophomore, Marshall averaged 8.1 points and 9.8 assists and shot 52.7 percent from the field. ==Professional playing career== ===2012 NBA draft=== On March 29, 2012, Marshall announced that he would enter the [[2012 NBA draft]] out of [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|UNC]] with three of his teammates: sophomore [[Harrison Barnes]], junior [[John Henson (basketball)|John Henson]] and senior [[Tyler Zeller]].{{cite news |last=Pickeral |first=Robbi |date=March 29, 2012 |title=Three UNC stars to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2012/story/_/id/7752253 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}} He was selected with the 13th overall pick in the 2012 NBA draft by the [[Phoenix Suns]]. ===Phoenix Suns (2012–2013)=== On July 16, 2012, Marshall signed a multi-year deal with the [[2012–13 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |date=July 16, 2012 |title=Suns sign Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8170658 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}} He joined the Suns for the 2012 NBA Summer League and in his first game, he had five assists and three steals.{{cite web |last=Seidlitz |first=Aaron |date=July 17, 2012 |title=Marshall Makes His Suns Debut |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/marshall_120717 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} In his final Summer League game, Marshall had a [[double-double]] with 15 points and 10 assists in a 96–87 victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/games/20120721/MEMPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Summer League: Suns 94, Grizzlies 87 |work=NBA.com |date=July 21, 2012 |access-date=November 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026221330/http://www.nba.com/summer-league/games/20120721/MEMPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=October 26, 2013 |url-status=dead }} On November 4, 2012, Marshall made his first official NBA appearance against the [[Orlando Magic]]. He did not record any statistics in that game. He had two assists and one steal in a blowout loss to the defending [[NBA Finals]] champion [[Miami Heat]] a day later. On November 29, 2012, the Suns assigned Marshall to the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA D-League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/phoenix_suns_assign_rookie_kendall_marshall_bakersfield_jam_2012_11_29.html|title=Phoenix Suns Assign Rookie Kendall Marshall to NBA D-League Affiliate Bakersfield Jam|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 29, 2012|date=November 22, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130202422/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/phoenix_suns_assign_rookie_kendall_marshall_bakersfield_jam_2012_11_29.html|archive-date=November 30, 2012}} In his first game in the D-League, Marshall recorded 21 points, 8 assists and 2 rebounds in a 102–95 victory over the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]]. Marshall was recalled by the Suns on December 21, 2012.{{cite web |date=December 21, 2012 |title=Marshall Recalled From D-League |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/marshall-recalled-d-league |access-date=December 21, 2012 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}} On February 5, 2013, Marshall recorded a season-high 11 points with 4 assists in a 96–90 victory against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. On March 9, 2013, Marshall had 9 points, 2 rebounds and 4 assists in a 107–105 victory over the [[Houston Rockets]]. Marshall's first official start in the NBA came on March 27, 2013, against the [[Utah Jazz]]. He had 13 assists in that game, his first game to record double-digit assists. In three starts, he totaled 37 assists.{{cite web |last=Resnick |first=Joe |date=2013-01-04 |title=Gasol, Marshall lead Lakers over Jazz 110-99 |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-gasol-marshall-lead-lakers-over-jazz-110-99-2014jan03-story.html |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On October 25, 2013, Marshall was traded, along with [[Marcin Gortat]], [[Shannon Brown]] and [[Malcolm Lee (basketball)|Malcolm Lee]], to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Emeka Okafor]] and a [[2014 NBA draft|2014 first-round draft]] pick.{{cite web |last=Hyman |first=Jeremy |date=October 25, 2013 |title=Wizards Acquire Gortat From Suns |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-gortat-suns |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} Marshall, Brown and Lee were all waived by the Wizards three days later.{{cite web |last=Hyman |first=Jeremy |date=October 28, 2013 |title=Wizards Waive Brown, Lee and Marshall |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-brown-lee-and-marshall |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} ===Delaware 87ers (2013)=== On December 3, 2013, Marshall was acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the NBA D-League.{{cite web |last=Shorr-Parks |first=Eliot |date=December 3, 2013 |title=Kendall Marshall claimed by Delaware 87ers, Sixers D-League team |url=https://www.nj.com/sixers/2013/12/kendall_marshall_signed_by_del_1.html |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NJ.com}} In his debut with Delaware, Marshall recorded 31 points, 10 assists, 9 rebounds and 2 steals in a 126–139 loss to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20131205/DELRGV/gameinfo.html|title=Vipers Stay Perfect With 139-126 Win Over Delaware|date=December 5, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=December 5, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131208065211/http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20131205/DELRGV/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 8, 2013}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2013–2014)=== On December 20, 2013, Marshall signed with the [[2013–14 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |date=December 20, 2013 |title=Lakers Sign Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/131220kendallmarshall |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} The injury-ravaged Lakers on January 3, 2014, made Marshall their sixth different player to start at point guard in [[2013–14 Los Angeles Lakers season|2013–14]], when he established career highs with 20 points and 15 assists in a 110–99 victory over Utah that snapped a six-game losing streak.{{cite news |title=Gasol, Marshall lead Lakers over Jazz 110-99 |date=January 3, 2014 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/tournament/2011/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=6224000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104205755/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/tournament/2011/columns/story?columnist=katz_andy&id=6224000 |archive-date=2014-01-04 |url-status=live }} It was his fourth career start. In his next game, he recorded a career high 17 assists in a loss to the Denver Nuggets. On July 18, 2014, Marshall was waived by the Lakers.{{cite web |last=Trudell |first=Mike |date=July 18, 2014 |title=Lakers Waive Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/140718marshall_waived |access-date=March 6, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2014–2015)=== On July 20, 2014, Marshall was claimed off waivers by the [[2014–15 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |date=July 20, 2014 |title=Bucks Awarded Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-awarded-kendall-marshall |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On January 17, 2015, he was ruled out for the rest of the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]] after suffering a torn anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee on January 15.{{cite web |date=January 17, 2015 |title=Kendall Marshall Injury Update |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/kendall-marshall-injury-update |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On February 19, 2015, Marshall was traded back to the Phoenix Suns in a three-team deal that also involved the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |last=Okada |first=C. |date=February 19, 2015 |title=Suns Acquire Brandon Knight in Three-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-acquire-brandon-knight-three-team-trade |access-date=March 6, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} He was subsequently waived by the Suns two days later alongside [[John Salmons]].{{cite web |last=Cunningham |first=Cody |date=February 21, 2015 |title=Suns Sign Barron to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-barron-10-day-contract |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2015–2016)=== On September 9, 2015, Marshall signed with the [[2015–16 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |date=September 9, 2015 |title=76ers sign point guard Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13619668 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}} On November 11, he was assigned to the Delaware 87ers in order to rehab his torn ACL.{{cite web |last=Pompey |first=Keith |date=November 11, 2015 |title=Sixers assign Wroten, Marshall to 87ers |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/blogs/sports/sixers/Sixers-assign-Wroten-Marshall-to-87ers.html |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=inquirer.com |via=The Philadelphia Inquirer}} On December 4, he was recalled by the 76ers.{{cite web |last=Feldman |first=Dan |date=December 4, 2015 |title=Tony Wroten and Kendall Marshall healthy, so 76ers waive Phil Pressey |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/tony-wroten-and-kendall-marshall-healthy-so-76ers-waive-phil-pressey |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=nbcsports.com}} He made his debut for the 76ers on December 11, recording 5 points and 6 assists as a starter in a loss to the Detroit Pistons.{{cite web |last=Gelston |first=Dan |date=December 11, 2015 |title=Pistons roll past woeful 76ers 107-95 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151211/DETPHI/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151214181111/http://www.nba.com/games/20151211/DETPHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=December 14, 2015 |access-date=December 11, 2015 |work=NBA.com}} On August 26, 2016, Marshall was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Tibor Pleiss]], two [[2017 NBA draft|2017 second-round draft]] picks and cash considerations.{{cite web |date=August 26, 2016 |title=Jazz waive Kendall Marshall after acquiring PG in trade with Sixers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/17397359 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=ESPN.com}} He was immediately waived by the Jazz upon being acquired.{{cite web |date=August 26, 2016 |title=Jazz Waive Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waive-kendall-marshall |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} ===Reno Bighorns (2016–2017)=== On November 29, 2016, Marshall was acquired by the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web |date=November 29, 2016 |title=Bighorns Acquire NBA Veteran Player Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/bighorns-acquire-nba-veteran-player-kendall-marshall/n-5218861 |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=oursportscentral.com}} ===Agua Caliente Clippers (2017)=== On September 21, 2017, Marshall signed a training camp contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |date=September 21, 2017 |title=Bucks Sign Kendall Marshall |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-kendall-marshall |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} He was waived by the Bucks on October 8, 2017, after appearing in three preseason games.{{cite web |date=October 8, 2017 |title=Kendall Marshall: Waived by Bucks |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kendall-marshall-waived-by-bucks |access-date=March 6, 2024 |work=cbssports.com}} Marshall signed with the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. After appearing in three games, Marshall opted to retire from basketball on November 23, 2017.{{cite web|last=Cockrum|first=Blake|url=https://keepingitheel.com/2017/11/23/unc-basketball-former-tar-heels-point-guard-kendall-marshall-retires/|title=Former Tar Heels point guard Kendall Marshall retires|work=KeepingItHeel.com|date=November 23, 2017|access-date=November 24, 2017|archive-date=December 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201033100/https://keepingitheel.com/2017/11/23/unc-basketball-former-tar-heels-point-guard-kendall-marshall-retires/|url-status=dead}} ==National team career== In August 2017, Marshall joined the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] for the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]],{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2017/08/americup-team-announced.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005160220/https://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2017/08/americup-team-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 5, 2017|title=USA Basketball Men's AmeriCup Team Announced|work=usab.com|date=August 21, 2017|access-date=October 8, 2017}} where he won a gold medal. ==Coaching career== Marshall resumed his studies at UNC in 2017–18, and graduated after the fall semester in December 2018. He also worked closely with the basketball team, who identified him as a student assistant coach by 2018–19.{{cite news|last=Martin|first=Ross|title=Kendall Marshall Graduates From UNC|date=December 17, 2018|work=247 Sports|url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/Kendall-Marshall-Graduates-UNC-Basketball-Coaching-Staff-126468302/|access-date=May 14, 2019}} On October 2, 2019, Tar Heels head coach [[Roy Williams (basketball coach)|Roy Williams]] named Marshall the director of recruiting, a newly created position on his staff.{{cite news|last=Trendel|first=Avery|title=Kendall Marshall Named UNC Men's Basketball Director of Recruiting|date=October 2, 2019|website=Chapelboro.com|url=https://chapelboro.com/sports/unc-sports/kendall-marshall-named-unc-mens-basketball-director-of-recruiting|access-date=April 18, 2020}} Marshall held that position until April 15, 2021, just after Williams' resignation.{{cite news|title=Davis Names Four Former Tar Heels To Basketball Staff|date=April 15, 2021|website=goheels.com|url=https://goheels.com/news/2021/4/15/mens-basketball-davis-names-four-former-tar-heels-to-basketball-staff.aspx|access-date=April 15, 2021}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
